user_questions.simulated_answer: 1) Stripe refunds API via a Named Credential, async; success -> Processing then Completed with processed date; failure -> Failed with error logged. 2) No preference; use your recommended default. 3) No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: The 'two wrong AskCoworker claims' rule fired early (D1 missed Pronto_Orders_API; D1/D2 wrong callout-after-insert claim), after which the skill says 'verify every AskCoworker fact you keep' but gives no guidance on whether to keep sending R/T at all; they then produced four more wrong platform claims (Automated Process user, one callout per Queueable, enqueueJob banned in batch/future, test will fail). R/T added little beyond test-method names.

User intent 'success -> Processing then Completed' cannot be literally met in a single Queueable (no DML before callout). The skill has no guidance for mapping a user-stated sequence onto a platform constraint; I recorded it as an assumption (Processing for Stripe 'pending', Completed for 'succeeded').

The requirement is undeliverable until creators supply the Stripe PaymentIntent ID, which would change three callers (two flows and an agent action schema). Step 5 says ask only if it defeats the main purpose; it arguably does, but I had already used the one question message and the rule for 'a later intent fork' is unclear about whether caller changes count; I marked it blocking for delivery instead.

The *I* split rule ('split I by responsibility') produced part 1 that proposed widening five permission sets including namespaced ones, contrary to design rules; the templates do not remind AskCoworker of the 'do not widen broad permission sets' rule.
org-verification.md has no note on Organization.DefaultCurrencyIsoCode being unavailable in single-currency orgs; the query failed and the currency assumption stayed unverified.

D2 template asks for 'record-triggered flows' so AskCoworker reported '0 flows' while missing autolaunched flows that create the record; the template could ask for all flows that create or update the objects.
